title: Socrates and the Kick
source: Diogenes Laertius, Lives of the Philosophers II.21 (Yonge tr.)
lesson: When someone acts like a donkey, you don't have to become one too.
lines: Socrates spent his days in the market, asking questions. And his questions made some people very, very angry.
One man could not win the argument. His face went red. His ears went hot. And then, he kicked Socrates!
Everyone gasped. Socrates! Aren't you going to take him to court? He kicked you, in front of everyone!
Socrates simply dusted off his robe, and thought about it for a moment.
Tell me, he said. If a donkey kicked me, would I take the donkey to court?
The crowd burst out laughing. The angry man stood there, looking very, very silly. Even the donkey looked embarrassed.
When someone acts like a donkey, you don't have to become one too. Stay calm, and let their behaviour speak for itself.
Next time: the ring that makes you invisible. Follow so you don't miss it!
